title: 12-name watchlist · 4 November 2026, 12:00 SGT
summary: New reports cover Tesla’s planned Korean FSD complaint, AMD’s conditional warrants and Berkshire’s reported Sirius XM purchases. The AMD report has an unresolved amount discrepancy against the issuer’s tables. Earlier AMD call remarks and the PacifiCorp appeal hearing are clearly labelled catch-up. Regular-close metrics and all six return horizons are unchanged. Separate saved after-hours observations include AMD $508.20 (+5.02%) and Tesla $391.53 (−1.75%) at 08:59 SGT, not live prices.
coverage_note: Review window: 4 November 2026, 08:00–12:00 SGT (00:00–04:00 UTC), with a 15-minute overlap from 07:45 SGT. Sources were rechecked after the fixed 12:00 SGT cutoff. The previous 08:00 SGT edition and all earlier research, reports and qualifications remain in their original archives. This incremental edition does not repeat unchanged prior events as new. News coverage remains partial, not a complete newswire census.
price_basis: All main prices are USD completed regular-session observations for 3 November 2026, at 16:00 EST (4 November 05:00 SGT), with their original individually recorded vendor timestamps. Daily change compares the 2 November ordinary close. Seconds supplied by Yahoo and minute precision supplied by Stock Analysis are preserved. These are saved closes, not live or exact 12:00 SGT prices. Separately labelled after-hours snapshots in each company’s notes are dated 3 November 19:59 EST (4 November 08:59 SGT), except Berkshire at 19:55 EST (08:55 SGT). Their changes compare the regular close, and none replaces a return endpoint. Premarket fields remain empty. TSM is the US-listed USD ADR.
return_basis: Cumulative return = 100 × (3 November 2026 adjusted close ÷ baseline adjusted close − 1). The 1–6 calendar-month baselines are 2 October, 3 September, 3 August, 2 July, 3 June and 1 May 2026. October 3 and May 3 fall on weekends; July 3 is the observed US Independence Day market holiday, so preceding sessions are used. All 72 dated inputs were independently checked. Adjusted closes incorporate split and dividend/distribution adjustments; ordinary previous closes remain separate. These are cumulative returns before fees and taxes, not six individual monthly returns.
caveats: All 12 completed closes, previous closes and 72 adjusted-close baseline inputs were freshly reconfirmed. Every daily, cumulative-return and separate after-hours percentage was independently recomputed. The regular-price and return fields remain unchanged from the previous edition.

After-hours prices have minute precision from Stock Analysis and are saved observations, not live quotes. The later Reuters reports do not establish what caused any earlier price move. Do not combine after-hours changes with regular-session changes or the adjusted-close return endpoints.

Direct Yahoo access was sometimes rate-limited. Accessible indexed Yahoo regional historical rows and public Stock Analysis/Quiver histories were used for verification. Stale or differently adjusted alternatives were rejected rather than mixed into the saved provider basis. Source links remain beside every baseline.

TSM’s historical inputs consistently retain Yahoo’s adjusted series, including 3 September at 415.89. Micron’s 2 July adjusted baseline remains 975.26; an alternative stale 975.41 observation was rejected.

AMD’s original release shows a $1.097 billion warrant-liability adjustment, while the new Reuters report says $1.07 billion. The discrepancy is unresolved and remains explicit; neither figure is treated as a new cash payment.

We could not independently verify a complete official AMD Q3 earnings-call transcript. The newly included 2027 call outlook is attributed to Reuters and labelled earlier catch-up, not a new announcement in this review window.
Watch only: no user holding, executed trade, buy call or recommendation is implied. No private diary, brokerage record, personal account information or restricted screenshot is included.
All 12 SEC recent-submission feeds rechecked after 04:00 UTC; only Berkshire Form 4 falls in overlap/main window. Not a full third-party filing census.

Reuters searches and accessible syndications are partial coverage, not a complete wire census. Some direct web opens failed; full direct HTML was obtained for the included Tesla, Berkshire and AMD reports.
Alphabet and Meta current IR release lists did not render sufficiently; Micron relocated news list was also empty. Microsoft source homepage did not expose a dated current list.
No newly verified event for quiet tickers does not establish that no news occurred. No generic filler added.
Prior AMD Q3 results, Meta dollar bond pricing, Amazon 13F and Apple Siri preview deduplicated rather than re-presented as new. No new Meta settlement confirmation verified.
No current user holdings, trades, recommendations or private information inferred. TSM coverage refers to the US-listed USD ADR.

rows.name: Berkshire Hathaway Class B

research.headline: New SEC filing: Berkshire reports Sirius XM purchases
facts: A Form 4 accepted at 02:30:04 UTC reports 743,965 Sirius XM shares purchased on 30 October, 66,968 on 2 November and 113,348 on 3 November: 924,281 shares in total.

The filing reports 125,731,398 shares afterward, including 109,746,508 held by GEICO and 15,984,890 in subsidiary pension plans. The filing includes ownership disclaimers for the pension-plan positions.
research.analysis: This is a disclosed Berkshire-related portfolio transaction, not a Berkshire operating-results release.
research.risks: The issuer is Sirius XM, not Berkshire. These are dated reported transactions and not evidence of current holdings or any user trade. Do not describe all reported shares as directly owned by Berkshire.
research.next_watch: Later ownership filings for additional changes.

research.headline: Overlap catch-up: Oregon court hears PacifiCorp wildfire appeal
facts: Reuters reports the Oregon Supreme Court heard arguments on 3 November over reviving a wildfire liability verdict after an appeals court set aside $1.25 billion in awards to 201 plaintiffs.
The report was published at 23:55:50 UTC, in the 15-minute overlap before this edition’s main window; it was not in the previous edition. No new decision is reported.
research.analysis: The appeal is a contingent legal-risk development for Berkshire’s utility operations, not a new damages award.
research.risks: Potential damages are uncertain; allegations and courtroom questions do not establish the eventual ruling or payout.
research.next_watch: Oregon Supreme Court ruling. Reuters says rulings typically take months; no exact decision date is verified.

rows.name: Advanced Micro Devices

research.headline: New Reuters warrant report: conditional dilution and a source-number discrepancy
facts: Reuters reports CFO Jean Hu said customer warrants begin diluting shareholders only after vesting and exercise conditions are met, with more timing guidance expected in 2027.

The original 3 November earnings release and SEC exhibit show a $1.097 billion fair-value warrant-liability adjustment, or $0.66 per share. Reuters instead reports $1.07 billion; that discrepancy is unresolved. The cash-flow statement separately adds back $1.179 billion of net non-cash customer-warrant impact.
research.analysis: Equity-linked customer incentives can create earnings volatility and future dilution alongside chip sales growth. The fair-value adjustment is not a cash outflow.
research.risks: Do not equate warrants with shares already issued or exercised. Do not silently replace the primary-source $1.097 billion with Reuters $1.07 billion or confuse it with the separate cash-flow addback.
research.next_watch: 2027 management guidance on vesting/exercise timing and future SEC disclosure.

research.headline: Earlier call catch-up: 2027 growth outlook and weaker PC-unit demand
facts: Reuters attributes to Lisa Su an expectation that overall 2027 revenue will grow more than 80%, with data-center chips supplying about 80% of sales.

Reuters also reports AMD expects PC unit shipments to decline by a double-digit percentage in 2027. These are earlier 3 November call remarks newly verified for this edition, not a new call after midnight UTC.
research.analysis: The outlook implies greater dependence on data-center demand while the PC market weakens.
research.risks: These are management forecasts, not realized results; supply, execution and customer concentration remain relevant. No after-hours percentage is carried over from the report.
research.next_watch: 2027 shipment execution and subsequent official call materials.

rows.name: Tesla

research.headline: New Reuters report: Korean consumer group plans FSD marketing complaint
facts: Reuters reports Citizens United for Consumer Sovereignty plans to file a complaint with the Korea Fair Trade Commission on 5 November, alleging Tesla marketed FSD for vehicles that could not legally use it.

A KFTC official told Reuters an investigation into FSD advertising began earlier this year and Tesla submitted written responses. Tesla did not respond to Reuters requests for comment. FSD requires active driver supervision.
research.analysis: A potential advertising restriction or certification delay could affect Korean software sales; this report does not quantify an earnings impact.
research.risks: These are allegations and a planned complaint, not a finding of liability or an imposed penalty. The number of customers who bought FSD on ineligible vehicles remains unclear.
research.next_watch: Whether the complaint is filed on 5 November; KFTC decisions, certification progress and Tesla response.
